metadata.title: Claude, Analyzing Financial Statements.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude analyzing a balance sheet is general financial judgment or something more specific, using the analyzing-financial-statements skill's own description as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that a financial-analysis skill is SKILL.md, a spec Claude reads and runs the same way against whatever statement you hand it.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (hand the skill a balance sheet: same three steps run every time; then the same pipeline runs identically twice, and just as readily against a statement outside the spec)

beats.narration_text: You'd guess someone teaches Claude to analyze financial statements. Nobody does — Claude wasn't trained on that. It's pointed at a folder it reads before it acts. Let's take that folder apart.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'How do I teach Claude to analyze financial statements?', hesitates on 'teach', corrects to 'point', lands the real question

beats.narration_text: Here's what's actually happening. The analyzing-financial-statements folder holds three files: calculate_ratios.py, interpret_ratios.py, and a two-kilobyte SKILL.md carrying every instruction in plain language — no hidden logic, no hidden judgment. Claude reads SKILL.md, then acts on the numbers. The file is the program; the model is just the interpreter.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder opening to three files, SKILL.md highlighted; 'not trained on it' callout; 'the file is the program' closer

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: A folder icon opens into three file rows: calculate_ratios.py (12k), interpret_ratios.py (16k), and SKILL.md (2k) — SKILL.md recolors teal and grows slightly. A 'not trained on it' tag crosses out a brain glyph. Closing line: 'the file is the program'.

beats.narration_text: The instructions live in a Steps section: read each step in order, execute it, return the result. Linear by design — no branching unless a step explicitly says branch. That constraint is the whole point. Watch the anchor. Hand it a balance sheet: it reads the numbers, runs calculate_ratios.py, hands back the ratios. Three steps, every time — the same three.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — three linear pipeline phases, then a balance sheet arrowing through calculate_ratios.py to a ratios output

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — a balance sheet, three steps
production_viz.mechanic: Three phase cards appear left to right and connect with arrows: 'read SKILL.md' / 'execute' / 'return result'. They fade back. THE ANCHOR. A card labelled 'balance sheet' arrows into a card labelled 'calculate_ratios.py', which arrows into a card labelled 'ratios out'. Closing line beneath: 'same three steps, every time'. THIS EXACT SEQUENCE RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: The anchor returns. Hand it the same balance sheet twice — calculate_ratios.py returns identical ratios both times. That's the payoff of a file being the program: deterministic behavior, not model judgment. Now the reverse. Hand it a statement the steps weren't written for, and it still runs those same three steps against numbers SKILL.md never named. It optimized for repeatability at the expense of range — only what the page names, nothing that isn't.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same pipeline firing identically twice, then split: identical statement twice = identical ratios; statement outside the spec = same steps still run

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same input, same output; then the limit
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 PIPELINE RETURNS, identical, running twice in a row — two matching 'ratios out' cards appear side by side, labelled 'same input, same output'. Then it splits: left card 'in-spec statement' → pipeline → clean ratios, labelled 'the payoff'; right card 'statement outside the spec' → the same pipeline → ratios computed anyway, labelled 'the limit'. Closing line: 'only what SKILL.md names'.

beats.narration_text: A financial-analysis skill isn't Claude reasoning about finance. It's SKILL.md — a spec Claude reads and runs the same way against whatever statement you hand it. The model doesn't judge; the file does.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini: I want to analyze financial statements for investment insights. Read the analyzing-financial-statements skill and walk me through what you'll do before you do it. That walk-through is the diagnostic — it surfaces the ratios it's about to run and the steps SKILL.md actually names, before any numbers move. Go deeper: hand it a statement the skill wasn't written for, and ask what changes. Liam, in for Bear.
